description: PRD-103: Verification & Quality — Full research + design PRD. Study LLM-as-judge patterns, constitutional AI critique, eval frameworks. Design the verification layer that validates task outputs against success criteria.

userStories.title: Research LLM-as-judge patterns
userStories.description: As a researcher, I need to study how LLMs evaluate other LLM outputs so that our verification is grounded in proven methodology
acceptanceCriteria: Study MT-Bench evaluation methodology — pairwise comparison, scoring rubrics, judge prompt design
Study Chatbot Arena / LMSYS — how human preferences are captured and correlated with LLM judges
Study Constitutional AI critique patterns — self-critique, revision chains
Study DeepEval framework — metrics, test cases, evaluation datasets
Study RAGAS for RAG evaluation — faithfulness, answer relevancy, context recall
Study OpenAI Evals framework — eval structure, grading functions
Comparison table: framework, what it evaluates, accuracy, cost, integration effort
Write to PRD section: '## 2. Prior Art: LLM Evaluation & Judging'
Include false positive/negative rates where available from literature
userStories.notes: PRD-100 Open Question #3: 'Can LLM-as-judge reliably assess task completion? What's the false positive rate?' This story answers that question. Use DeepWiki for deepeval (confident-ai/deepeval), ragas (explodinggradients/ragas).

userStories.title: Research FutureAGI integration opportunities
userStories.description: As a researcher, I need to understand what FutureAGI already provides so that we don't rebuild evaluation capabilities that exist
acceptanceCriteria: Read existing FutureAGI integration code in the Automatos codebase
Document what eval types FutureAGI supports: prompt scanning, output evaluation, hallucination detection
Identify which FutureAGI capabilities map to mission verification needs
Define integration strategy — use FutureAGI for what it does well, build custom for what it doesn't cover
Write to PRD section: '## 3. FutureAGI Integration'
Include API call examples for FutureAGI eval in mission context
userStories.notes: FutureAGI is already in the codebase — search for 'futureagi' or 'fi_' imports. Don't propose adding a new eval framework if FutureAGI already handles the use case. Extend, don't replace.

userStories.title: Design verification taxonomy
userStories.description: As a platform architect, I need a verification taxonomy so that different task types get appropriate quality checks
acceptanceCriteria: Define verification dimensions: completeness, accuracy, format compliance, relevance, consistency
Map task_types (from PRD-101) to verification strategies: research → factual accuracy + completeness, writing → quality + format, coding → correctness + tests, analysis → logic + evidence
Define scoring rubric: 1-5 scale with clear definitions for each level
Define pass/fail thresholds — configurable per mission autonomy level
Write to PRD section: '## 4. Verification Taxonomy'
Include rubric examples for 3 different task types
userStories.notes: The existing report grading (PRD-76) uses star ratings 1-5. Align the verification scoring with this existing pattern so the UI doesn't need separate display logic.

userStories.title: Design verifier service
userStories.description: As a platform architect, I need the VerifierService designed with clear interfaces and integration with the coordinator
acceptanceCriteria: Define VerifierService class with methods: verify_task_output(task_id, output, criteria) → VerificationResult
Define VerificationResult: score (float), passed (bool), feedback (str), suggestions (list), dimensions (dict of dimension → score)
Define verifier prompt template — structured evaluation prompt with rubric injection
Define model selection — verifier should use a DIFFERENT model than the task executor (diversity principle)
Define integration with coordinator — when coordinator calls verifier, what happens on pass vs fail
Write to PRD section: '## 5. VerifierService Design'
Include sequence diagram for verify → pass and verify → fail → retry flows
Address: verification cost budget — verifier calls cost tokens too
userStories.notes: The verifier is NOT an agent — it's a service like the coordinator. It uses an LLM call but doesn't go through AgentFactory. Keep it simple: structured prompt → LLM → parse response → VerificationResult. No tool calling needed for verification.

userStories.title: Design success criteria specification
userStories.description: As a platform architect, I need a way for users and coordinators to specify what 'done' looks like for each task
acceptanceCriteria: Define success criteria format — structured (checklist) vs natural language vs hybrid
Define how coordinator generates criteria during task decomposition
Define how users can override/add criteria at mission creation
Define criteria types: output_format, content_requirements, quality_threshold, constraints
Connect to orchestration_tasks schema (PRD-101) — where criteria are stored
Write to PRD section: '## 6. Success Criteria Specification'
Include 3 examples of well-formed criteria for different task types
Address: overly strict criteria causing unnecessary failures
userStories.notes: Keep criteria simple. A list of strings with a threshold (e.g., 'pass if 4/5 criteria met') is better than a complex schema. The coordinator generates these during planning — they need to be LLM-writable.

userStories.title: Design cross-agent consistency verification
userStories.description: As a platform architect, I need a way to verify consistency across tasks in a mission so that outputs don't contradict each other
acceptanceCriteria: Define consistency check triggers — when does cross-task verification happen
Define consistency dimensions: factual alignment, terminology consistency, conclusion coherence
Design lightweight consistency check — compare key claims across task outputs using embeddings or LLM
Address: cost of cross-task verification scales O(n²) — mitigation strategies
Write to PRD section: '## 7. Cross-Agent Consistency'
Include example: research agent says X, writer agent says not-X — how detected and resolved
userStories.notes: This is a Phase 2 stretch goal — don't over-design. A simple 'final review' step where the verifier reads all task outputs together is probably sufficient. Save the semantic field approach for Phase 3 (PRD-108).

userStories.title: Write PRD-103 opening and synthesis
userStories.description: As a document author, I need to write the complete PRD-103 document synthesizing all verification research
acceptanceCriteria: Create docs/PRDS/103-VERIFICATION-QUALITY.md
Header: version, type, status, priority, dependencies (PRD-100, PRD-101, PRD-102)
Section 1: Problem Statement
Synthesize US-001 through US-006 into coherent narrative
Include 'Design Decisions Made' table
Include 'What This PRD Delivers' and 'What This PRD Does NOT Cover'

userStories.title: Write PRD-103 conclusion and implementation artifacts
userStories.description: As a document author, I need to close PRD-103 with implementation-ready artifacts
acceptanceCriteria: Write '## 8. Verifier Prompt Templates' — actual prompt text for different verification types
Write '## 9. Risk Register'
Write '## 10. Implementation Acceptance Criteria'
Write '## 11. Appendix: VerifierService Interface' — Python class stub
Write '## 12. Appendix: VerificationResult Schema' — dataclass definition
Final review pass
PRD-103 complete and ready for peer review
userStories.notes: The verifier prompts are the key deliverable — they need to be production-quality, not sketches.
